articles.summary: Supreme Court Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson ripped her colleagues for fast-tracking cases on the high court’s emergency docket, saying "it has been noticeably less restrained, especially with respect to pending cases that involve controversial matters." The emergency docket, sometimes known as the shadow or interim docket, allows parties to ask the Supreme Court to quickly intervene in lawsuits and temporarily pause lower court rulings. The process can take a couple of days, weeks or months, and is viewed as a much speedier, although temporary, way to secure court relief than when the court fully considers the merits of a case, which can include a long briefing schedule and oral arguments. "Why is it that one party should get a fast pass to the Supreme Court of the United States, when so many other parties are queued up, waiting patiently for the court’s attention?" Jackson said Thursday during a speech at the University of the District of Columbia’s law school, according to The Hill . "If we’re not careful, the emergency docket can and will become an end run around the standard review process, a special avenue that certain privileged litigants can use selectively," she added. Summit meetings between the American president and his counterparts from Moscow and Beijing are particularly tricky because of the innately tense relationship between two adversaries. Mert Alas & Marcus Piggott; TAS Rights Management On Friday, Taylor Swift released "The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore." The "Showgirl" deluxe edition includes four new songs that Swift wrote after the original's release. "Patient Zero" and "Babylon" are standouts, but "Cleveland!" is one of her worst songs to date. Precious few music critics would've said that Taylor Swift's "The Life of a Showgirl" needed more songs. When it was unveiled last October, Swift's 12th studio album — inspired by the joy, drama, and "effervescence" of the Eras Tour , Swift said at the time — received some of the most disenchanted reviews of her career. Although "Showgirl" became a titanic commercial success , and some reviewers praised the album as glitzy and triumphant, many said it fell short of her best work as a songwriter. Even among Swifties, the pop star's ever-devoted fan base, "Showgirl" is commonly considered a bottom-tier album in her two-decade oeuvre. And yet, Swift has rarely been one to back down from a challenge. Faced with both thoughtful critiques and bad-faith smear campaigns , she refused to disavow "Showgirl."
